ledger.claim: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances, which is the only measure POL-RD-22 allows: 24.8 km actually driven less 20.5 km on the recommended route is 4.30 km. That is more than four times POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, so the trip is outside tolerance and the rider's overcharge complaint is made out on the record itself.

The driver never informed the rider of the deviation, as POL-RD-21 requires, before or at the point of deviation. The chat log shows the rider raising the route herself at 13:24 — 'are we going the right way? This doesn't look like the usual route to the airport' — and the driver answering only 'Don't worry, I know the way. We will reach on time.' That is not notice of a route change, gives no reason for it, and comes after the deviation had begun; no earlier driver message mentions traffic or a reroute. There is no acknowledgment by the rider, so the deviation was not agreed.

On these facts POL-RD-24(b) applies — traffic-justified reroute, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km — and the whole excess distance fare is refunded. I do not need to fight POL-RD-23: the PIE vehicle fire and the airport-exit congestion both intersect the recommended route and overlap the trip window, so the traffic limb is met on the data. Even if the judge read the reroute as not traffic-justified, POL-RD-24(d) refunds the whole excess distance fare too. The rider's recovery is the same 3.44 SGD on either row; the one row that would deny any refund, POL-RD-24(a), requires the rider to have been informed and to have agreed, and the chat log forecloses it.

The amount follows POL-RD-24's formula with no surge: 4.30 km x 0.80 SGD per km = 3.44 SGD, rounded to the cent. I rely on the fare breakdown only for the 0.80 SGD per-kilometre rate and the 35.00 SGD aggregate it states, and I disclose that this artifact is impaired — PARTIAL_RECORD, weight 0.75, because the ledger itemised no lines. That impairment goes to itemisation, not to the rate or the aggregate the ledger does state, and the deviation distance it multiplies comes from the trip record at full weight.

The rider filed this dispute, so under POL-GEN-03 a return of part of the trip's charge runs to the rider: PARTIAL_REFUND is part of the trip's charge returned to the filing party. The fare breakdown shows refund_issued_sgd of 0.0 — the rider has received nothing so far — and I disclose that artifact's impairment again: PARTIAL_RECORD, weight 0.75. The 3.44 SGD is therefore still owing, not already paid.

This case needs no human and no escalation. The contested amount is 6.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence; both parties' fraud_flags are 0, so the 0.95 threshold never engages; and POL-RD-25's 2 km limb is expressly switched off — route_deviation.thresholds.ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false — so the 4.30 km deviation does not force escalation. The facts POL-GEN-26 would require a rule to have — deviation distance, notification, fare — are all established above.

The GPS trace is impaired and I disclose it rather than lean on it: it carries LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, weight 0.8, with ten of fifteen intervals exceeding the version-7 policy's 120 s limb. It does not carry this side's case — POL-RD-22 forbids re-measuring the route from a sparse trace, and the deviation is taken from the trip record's two recorded distances, not from the trace. The trace is cited only as the record of which route was taken and when.

The reroute was traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. EV-ADVIS-00902-01 records a HIGH-severity VEHICLE_FIRE on the PIE eastbound, lanes 1 and 2 blocked, active 13:05-13:50, marked as intersecting the recommended route; EV-ADVIS-00902-02 records HEAVY_CONGESTION on the PIE's Changi Airport exit ramp, active 13:15-13:40, likewise intersecting the recommended route. Both overlap the trip window (13:15-13:52) and both types are ones POL-RD-23 admits (incident and congestion). POL-RD-21's opening words permit a driver to reroute in response to real-time traffic, congestion or a closure, so the driver's decision to leave the PIE corridor was a permitted response to a fire and heavy congestion on that corridor, and the case falls in POL-RD-24's traffic-justified rows rather than in the unjustified-detour framing the rider's claim advances.

The driver's justification is not carried by EV-ADVIS-00902-03, and that advisory neither supports nor defeats the reroute: its type is TRAFFIC_FLOW, which POL-RD-23 does not admit, and it is recorded as not intersecting the recommended route, so by its own terms it justifies nothing. The POL-RD-23 justification rests solely on the two PIE advisories, each of which satisfies the clause.

The driver concedes the deviation and does not argue the trip was within tolerance. POL-RD-22 measures it from the platform's own recorded distances - 24.8 km actual against 20.5 km recommended, a 4.30 km deviation - which exceeds the 1.0 km tolerance, and the same clause says the trace is not used to re-measure the distance because a sparse trace understates a route's length. There is therefore no route to POL-RD-24 rows (c) or (e) for the driver. EV-GPS-00902 is impaired (LOW_SAMPLE_RATE, weight 0.8) and the driver cites it only for that prohibition, not for any distance of its own.

The 6.50 SGD the rider asks back is not a measure POL-RD-24 provides: it is the gap between the total charged and the quoted estimate (35.00 against 28.50). The policy's measure of the excess is the deviation distance at the per-kilometre rate, 4.30 km x 0.80 SGD = 3.44 SGD, and the threshold block applies no surge to it. On the rider's best case the recoverable excess is 3.44 SGD; the balance of the 6.50 SGD claim fails. EV-FARE-00902 is impaired (PARTIAL_RECORD, weight 0.75 - the ledger itemises no lines), and the driver cites it for the charged total, the quoted estimate and the per-km rate only, not as a clean itemisation.

On POL-RD-21's notification limb the driver puts its case no higher than row (b) of POL-RD-24. The messages during the trip are two entries: the rider asking at 13:24 whether they were going the right way, and the driver answering at 13:25 that he knew the way and they would arrive on time. That answer gave no reason for the route, so the driver does not assert that POL-RD-21 was satisfied or that the rider agreed - row (a) is not open. What the same record does show is that the rider knew the route differed while the trip ran, raised it in-app, was answered within a minute, and stayed in the trip to Changi T3. On that footing the remedy is the excess distance fare of 3.44 SGD under row (b), never a refund of the trip fare and never 6.50 SGD.

Even if row (b) were held to apply, no partial refund can issue at the confidence POL-RD-25 requires, and the case must escalate. POL-GEN-02(2) caps the judge's confidence at the lowest weight among the artifacts carrying the deciding fact, and the money in issue is the excess distance fare, whose per-kilometre rate is carried only by EV-FARE-00902 - an artifact impaired at 0.75 on PARTIAL_RECORD, with no line items exported and the 0.80 rate read out of a note. 0.75 is below POL-RD-25's 0.80 threshold for an AI ruling on a route deviation; POL-GEN-22's 'final at any confidence' band below 10.00 SGD does not displace that, because POL-RD-25 adds the category's own rule on top of it. Under POL-RD-25 and POL-GEN-26 the case therefore goes to human review, and under POL-GEN-03 an escalation issues no monetary outcome: the 35.00 fare stands charged and the amount is held, nothing having been refunded (refund_issued_sgd 0.00).

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the rider's route-deviation complaint is made out on the merits, but the AI cannot issue the refund this dispute warrants, so the case goes to a human reviewer and the 6.50 SGD contested is held, neither collected nor refunded. Here is why, limb by limb. (1) The deviation: POL-RD-22 takes it from the platform's own recorded distances — 24.8 km driven against 20.5 km on the recommended route (EV-TRIP-00902, weight 1.0) — which is 4.30 km, over four times the 1.0 km tolerance; the sparse GPS trace (EV-GPS-00902) is not used to re-measure distance, as POL-RD-22 itself says. (2) Traffic justification: the reroute was justified under POL-RD-23 by the two PIE advisories — EV-ADVIS-00902-01 (HIGH-severity vehicle fire, an 'incident' type) and EV-ADVIS-00902-02 (HEAVY_CONGESTION at the airport exit) — each of which intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window; EV-ADVIS-00902-03 (ECP, TRAFFIC_FLOW, no intersection) justifies nothing and is neutral. (3) Notification: the driver did not inform the rider of the deviation as POL-RD-21 requires — the chat log (EV-CHAT-00902, weight 1.0) shows the rider raising the route herself at 13:24 and the driver replying only that he knew the way — so the deviation was not agreed. (4) On those facts POL-RD-24 row (b) applies (traffic-justified, rider not informed, deviation over 1 km), and the excess distance fare is 4.30 km x 0.80 SGD per km = 3.44 SGD, per POL-RD-24 and its no-surge threshold; the 6.50 SGD asked (the 35.00 charged less the 28.50 quote) is not a measure the policy provides, so the balance of that claim fails. (5) The obstacle is confidence. The 0.80 per-km rate is carried only by the fare breakdown, EV-FARE-00902, which is impaired at weight 0.75 (PARTIAL_RECORD — the ledger exported no line items). Under POL-GEN-02(2) my confidence is capped at that 0.75, and POL-RD-25 permits an AI ruling on a route deviation only at a confidence of 0.80 or more. The 6.50 SGD value is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, but POL-RD-25 adds the category's own 0.80 threshold on top of POL-GEN-22, and the code fixes this case's required confidence at 0.80. At 0.75 I fall short. POL-RD-25 therefore escalates the case: no monetary outcome issues now, the 35.00 SGD fare stands charged, the rider has received nothing (refund_issued_sgd 0.00), and the reviewer has the open question of whether to award the 3.44 SGD excess distance fare that the merits support but this confidence bar prevents me from ordering.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
